facts.statement: Knoetschkesuchus is a small atoposaurid crocodylomorph that lived during the Late Jurassic in Germany and Portugal.
facts.quote: Knoetschkesuchus is a genus of small atoposaurid crocodylomorph from the Late Jurassic of Germany and Portugal.

facts.statement: Knoetschkesuchus was a small, short-snouted crocodilian measuring approximately 55 cm in length.
facts.quote: Knoetschkesuchus was a small and short-snouted crocodilian, measuring about 55 cm in length

facts.statement: Knoetschkesuchus primarily fed on small prey such as invertebrates, amphibians, and mammals.
facts.quote: that primarily fed on small prey, including invertebrates, amphibians, and mammals

facts.statement: The species Knoetschkesuchus guimarotae was named based on over 400 specimens, including several partial skeletons.
facts.quote: K. guimarotae, named from over 400 specimens including several partial skeletons

facts.statement: Knoetschkesuchus is distinguished from other atoposaurids by having only two distinct types of teeth and lacking leaf-shaped teeth.
facts.quote: Knoetschkesuchus only has two distinct types of teeth, lacking the leaf-shaped teeth seen in other atoposaurids

facts.statement: Fossils of Knoetschkesuchus langenbergensis were found in the Langenberg Quarry in the Harz Mountains near Goslar, Lower Saxony, Germany.
facts.quote: located within the Langenberg Quarry in the Harz Mountains near Goslar, Lower Saxony, Germany

facts.statement: The deposits containing Knoetschkesuchus langenbergensis fossils date to the Upper Kimmeridgian stage of the Jurassic.
facts.quote: These deposits have been dated to the Upper Kimmeridgian stage of the Jurassic

facts.statement: Knoetschkesuchus langenbergensis was described in a 2017 paper by Daniela Schwarz, Maik Raddatz, and Oliver Wings.
facts.quote: described in a 2017 paper published by Daniela Schwarz, Maik Raddatz, and Oliver Wings

facts.statement: The genus name Knoetschkesuchus honors Nils Knötschke, a researcher at the Dinosaurier-Freilichtmuseum Münchehagen responsible for the Langenberg Quarry specimens.
facts.quote: The genus name Knoetschkesuchus combines the family name of Nils Knötschke, a researcher at the DFMMh who was responsible for the collection, curation, and preparation of Langenberg Quarry specimens

facts.statement: Knoetschkesuchus guimarotae originates from the lignite layers of the Guimarota quarry near Leiria, Portugal.
facts.quote: K. guimarotae originates from the lignite layers of the Guimarota quarry, located near Leiria, Portugal

facts.statement: The Guimarota strata containing K. guimarotae fossils have been dated to the Kimmeridgian based on fossil ostracods.
facts.quote: which has been dated to the Kimmeridgian on the basis of fossil ostracods

facts.statement: Some specimens of K. guimarotae show marks of scavenging.
facts.quote: Some specimens show the marks of scavenging

facts.statement: Both species of Knoetschkesuchus were quadrupedal with long and slender limbs.
facts.quote: Typical of the group, both species were quadrupedal, bearing long and slender limbs

facts.statement: Each osteoderm of Knoetschkesuchus bears a longitudinal keel, which is less developed in K. langenbergensis than in K. guimarotae.
facts.quote: Each osteoderm bears a keel running longitudinally, although the keels are less-developed in K. langenbergensis

facts.statement: The skull of Knoetschkesuchus is relatively short, with the snout comprising 47% of skull length in K. langenbergensis and 42% in K. guimarotae.
facts.quote: The skull of Knoetschesuchus is relatively short, with the snout taking up 47% of skull length in K. langenbergensis and 42% in K. guimarotae

facts.statement: The short snout of Knoetschkesuchus allows it to be classified as a brevirostrine crocodilian.
facts.quote: which allows them to be classified as brevirostrine crocodilians

facts.statement: The oval-shaped antorbital fenestra in Knoetschkesuchus is small, measuring only 9% of the eye socket's length.
facts.quote: The oval-shaped antorbital fenestra is small, being only 9% the length of the eye socket

facts.statement: The presence of the antorbital fenestra is unique to both species of Knoetschkesuchus among atoposaurids.
facts.quote: its presence is unique to both species of the genus among atoposaurids

facts.statement: Both species of Knoetschkesuchus were formerly classified as belonging to the genus Theriosuchus.
facts.quote: Both species were formerly recognized as belonging to Theriosuchus

facts.statement: The pterygoid bone at the bottom of the Knoetschkesuchus skull is approximately twice as wide as it is long.
facts.quote: On the bottom of the skull, the pterygoid is about twice as wide as it is long.

facts.statement: A ridge formed by a projection on the front of the pterygoid bone has furrow-like depressions on either side that contain the choanae.
facts.quote: At the front of the pterygoid is a small projection that extends backwards to form a ridge, on either side of which is a furrow-like depression (the choanal groove) containing the choanae.

facts.statement: When viewed from the side, the basisphenoid bone resembles a triangular hatchet in shape.
facts.quote: The basisphenoid resembles a triangular hatchet in shape when viewed from the side.

facts.statement: The side of the dentary bone is pitted, with the pits being much denser in K. langenbergensis than in K. guimarotae.
facts.quote: The side of the dentary is pitted, albeit much more densely so in K. langenbergensis.

facts.statement: Both species of Knoetschkesuchus possess only two distinct types of teeth, a trait unique among atoposaurids.
facts.quote: Both species of Knoetschkesuchus have only two distinct types of teeth, uniquely among atoposaurids.

facts.statement: Both species have five premaxillary teeth, with the fourth being about one-third larger than the others.
facts.quote: There are 5 premaxillary teeth in both species, the fourth of which is about a third larger relative to the others.

facts.statement: The maxilla has 12 distinct sockets in K. langenbergensis.
facts.quote: The maxilla has 12 distinct sockets in K. langenbergensis.

facts.statement: The dentary exhibits 21 teeth in K. langenbergensis and at least 20 in K. guimarotae.
facts.quote: Meanwhile, the dentary exhibits 21 teeth in K. langenbergensis and at least 20 in K. guimarotae.

facts.statement: Specimens of K. langenbergensis were first preliminarily described in a 2006 paper by Hans-Volker Karl et al. and initially referred to the genus Theriosuchus.
facts.quote: When the known specimens of K. langenbergensis were first described in a preliminary fashion by a 2006 paper from Hans-Volker Karl et al., they were referred to the genus Theriosuchus.

facts.statement: In 2016, Mark Young et al. criticized previous diagnoses of Theriosuchus, noting that many characters were widely distributed among Atoposauridae, difficult to assess, or not present at all.
facts.quote: In 2016 Mark Young et al. criticized these diagnoses, noting that many characters were either more widely distributed among the Atoposauridae, difficult to assess, or—in the case of the latter diagnosis—not present at all.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis consistently found that Atoposauridae, represented by Knoetschkesuchus, Theriosuchus, and Alligatorium, forms a monophyletic clade.
facts.quote: The phylogenetic trees recovered by this analysis consistently found that Atoposauridae, represented by Knoetschkesuchus, Theriosuchus, and Alligatorium, forms a monophyletic clade.

facts.statement: K. langenbergensis differs from the proposed Theriosuchus diagnosis in four out of nine traits, a difference cited by Schwarz et al. as the basis for separating Knoetschkesuchus into its own genus.
facts.quote: K. langenbergensis differs from this diagnosis in four out of nine traits, which Schwarz et al. cited as a basis for both the generic separation of Knoetschkesuchus and the necessity of revising the diagnosis further.

facts.statement: Knoetschkesuchus was a small predator that primarily ate invertebrates and possibly small vertebrates like amphibians and mammals.
facts.quote: Being relatively small, Knoetschkesuchus would have mainly fed on invertebrates and possibly small vertebrates (including amphibians and mammals).

facts.statement: During the Kimmeridgian, Europe consisted of scattered archipelagos surrounded by the shallow inland Tethys Ocean.
facts.quote: During the Kimmeridgian, Europe was covered by the shallow inland Tethys Ocean, with exposed landmasses being a series of scattered archipelagos.

facts.statement: The Langenberg Quarry where K. langenbergensis was found is located in the Lower Saxony Basin, associated with the Rhenisch, Bohemian, and London-Brabant Massifs.
facts.quote: The Langenberg Quarry, where K. langenbergensis is known from, is part of the Lower Saxony Basin, which would have been part of the landmass associated with the Rhenisch, Bohemian, and London-Brabant Massifs.

facts.statement: Although the Langenberg Quarry was a shallow marine environment during the Kimmeridgian, K. langenbergensis was likely not marine because its fossils were transported from nearby islands.
facts.quote: During the Kimmeridgian, it would have been a shallow marine environment; however, this does not imply that K. langenbergensis was marine, since the animals and plants of the Langenberg Quarry were probably transported allochthonously (albeit only by a short distance) from the surrounding islands.

facts.statement: The Guimarota locality where K. guimarotae was found is in the eastern Lusitanian Basin, part of the Iberian Meseta.
facts.quote: The Guimarota locality is located in the eastern Lusitanian Basin, which is part of the Iberian Meseta.

facts.statement: Two species of Knoetschkesuchus are known: K. langenbergensis described by Schwartz et al. in 2017, and K. guimarotae originally classified as Theriosuchus guimarotae.
facts.quote: Se conocen dos especies: la especie alemana K. langenbergensis, descrita por Schwartz et al. en 2017 con base en dos esqueletos parciales y varios huesos aislados; y la especie portuguesa K. guimarotae, nombrada de tres cráneos parciales así como varios otros elementos, y fue clasificada originalmente como una especie de Theriosuchus.

facts.statement: The fossils of K. langenbergensis include a partial adult skeleton with a skull, a complete juvenile skull, an isolated angular bone, an isolated left dentary, an isolated femur, an isolated metatarsal, and a partial skeleton with osteoderms, vertebrae, and ribs.
facts.quote: Estos incluyen: el espécimen holotipo DFMMh/FV 200, el esqueleto parcial de un adulto con un cráneo; DFMMh/FV 605, el cráneo completo de un juvenil; DFMMh/FV 261, un hueso angular aislado; DFMMh/FV 790.12, un dentario izquierdo aislado; DFMMh/FV 279, un fémur aislado; DFMMh/FV 790.11, metatarso aislado; y DFMMh/FV 325, un esqueleto parcial que incluye osteodermos, vértebras y costillas.

facts.statement: Knoetschkesuchus specimens are housed at the Dinosaurier-Freilichtmuseum Münchehagen in Rehburg-Loccum, Germany.
facts.quote: Los especímenes pertenecientes a Knoetschkesuchus son alojados en el Dinosaurier-Freilichtmuseum Münchehagen (por ello son etiquetados con la sigla DFMMh/FV) en Rehburg-Loccum, Alemania.

facts.statement: The genus Knoetschkesuchus was established by Schwarz et al. in 2017.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Schwarz et al., 2017

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Knoetschkesuchus is K. langenbergensis.
facts.quote: type_species: Knoetschkesuchus langenbergensis

facts.statement: The two species of Knoetschkesuchus are K. langenbergensis and K. guimarotae, the latter originally named Theriosuchus guimarotae.
facts.quote: subdivision: K. langenbergensis Schwartz et al., 2017 (tipo) K. guimarotae (Schwarz & Salisbury, 2005) (originalmente Theriosuchus guimarotae)

facts.statement: Knoetschkesuchus is an extinct atoposaurid eusuchian crocodyliform that lived during the Late Jurassic in Germany and Portugal.
facts.quote: Knoetschkesuchus es un género de extinto de crocodilomorfo eusuquio atoposáurido que vivió durante el Jurásico Superior en Alemania y Portugal.

facts.statement: Both species of Knoetschkesuchus functioned as small predators ecologically distinct from other contemporary crocodilians, likely originating through dispersal over larger landmasses.
facts.quote: The two species of Knoetschkesuchus were part of similar faunas, in both of which they functioned as small predators ecologically partitioned from the other contemporary crocodilians; it is likely that these faunas originated through dispersal over larger landmasses.

facts.statement: Some researchers have attributed specimens assigned to K. langenbergensis to another species of Theriosuchus, T. pusillus.
facts.quote: Los especímenes atribuidos a K. langenbergensis también habían sido atribuidos a otra especie de Theriosuchus, T. pusillus por algunos investigadores.

facts.statement: Researchers Schwarz and colleagues assigned the species K. guimarotae to the genus Knoetschkesuchus, noting it was originally classified as a species of Theriosuchus.
facts.quote: Schwarz y colaboradores también asignaron una especie adicional a Knoetschkesuchus, K. guimarotae, la cual fue clasificada originalmente como una especie de Theriosuchus.

facts.statement: The species K. guimarotae originates from lignite layers found in the Guimarota quarry near Leiría, Portugal.
facts.quote: K. guimarotae se origina de las capas de lignita de la cantera de Guimarota, localizada cerca de Leiría, Portugal.

facts.statement: The geological formations containing K. guimarotae have been dated to the Kimmeridgian stage based on fossil ostracods.
facts.quote: Estas han sido asignadas a la Formación Alcobaça, una subunidad de la Formación Abadia, la cual ha sido datada del Kimmeridgiense con base en sus ostrácodos fósiles.

facts.statement: Fossils of K. guimarotae are housed at the Institute of Geosciences of the Free University of Berlin.
facts.quote: Los restos de K. guimarotae están alojados en el Instituto de Ciencias Geológicas de la Universidad Libre de Berlín (de ahí su sigla de IPFUB).

facts.statement: Some specimens show evidence of having been scavenged by other animals.
facts.quote: Algunos de estos muestran marcas de haber sido devorados por carroñeros.

facts.statement: K. guimarotae was very small, reaching a maximum length of only 55 centimeters.
facts.quote: Como ocurre con otros miembros de Atoposauridae, Knoetschkesuchus era muy pequeño; la especie K. guimarotae solo medía 55 centímetros en su máxima longitud.

facts.statement: The backs of both species were covered with two rows of rectangular bony osteoderms that were wider than they were long.
facts.quote: Los dorsos de ambas especies están cubiertos con dos filas de osteodermos óseos rectangulares, centrados hacia el eje medio, los cuales son más anchos que largos.

facts.statement: Each osteoderm carried a longitudinal keel, though these keels were less developed in K. langenbergensis.
facts.quote: Cada osteodermo lleva una quilla que corre en sentido longitudinal, aunque las quillas están menos desarrolladas en K. langenbergensis.

facts.statement: In K. guimarotae, tail osteoderms had high, sharp keels and were longer than wide, unlike other osteoderms, and were domed.
facts.quote: Al menos en K. guimarotae, los osteodermos de la cola tenían quillas altas y afiladas; aquellos cerca de la parte posterior de la cola tendían a ser más largos que anchos, a diferencia de otros osteodermos, y además estaban abovedados.

facts.statement: The skull was relatively short, with the snout comprising 47% of the cranial length in K. langenbergensis and 42% in K. guimarotae.
facts.quote: El cráneo de Knoetschesuchus era relativamente corto, con un hocico que comprendía el 47% de la longitud craneana de K. langenbergensis y el 42% en K. guimarotae.

facts.statement: The upward-facing nostrils were clearly separated by the nasals in K. guimarotae, but this separation is unclear in K. langenbergensis.
facts.quote: Las narinas, que se orientan hacia arriba, están claramente separadas por los nasales en K. guimarotae, pero no es claro que ese sea el caso en K. langenbergensis.

facts.statement: The oval anteorbital fenestra was very small, only 9% of the eye orbit length, and its presence in both species is a unique trait among atoposaurids.
facts.quote: La fenestra anteorbital en forma de óvalo es muy pequeña, con solo el 9% de la longitud de la órbita ocular; su presencia en ambas especies del género es un rasgo único entre los atoposáuridos.

facts.statement: The eye orbit was large and oval, being 54% longer than it was high.
facts.quote: Entretanto, la órbita ocular es grande y ovalada, siendo 54% más larga que alta.

facts.statement: The postorbital had two rami joining in a slight curve, separated by an angle of 130 degrees in K. langenbergensis.
facts.quote: El postorbital tiene dos ramos que se unen en una discreta curva, separados por un ángulo de 130° en K. langenbergensis.

facts.statement: In the lower skull region, the pterygoid was nearly twice as wide as it was long.
facts.quote: En la zona inferior del cráneo, el pterigoideo es cerca del doble de ancho que de largo.

facts.statement: In the related genus Theriosuchus, the choanae were immersed in a wide depression resembling a bowl.
facts.quote: En Theriosuchus, las coanas se hallan inmersas en una depresión ancha que recuerda un cuenco.

facts.statement: In K. guimarotae, the two halves of the dentary diverge at an angle of 20 degrees near the front and widen to 40 degrees further back.
facts.quote: En K. guimarotae, las dos mitades del dentario divergen la una de la otra en un ángulo de 20° cerca del frente, y pasa a ser de 40° más hacia atrás.

facts.statement: The presence of an oval-shaped external mandibular fenestra is a unique characteristic of this genus among atoposaurids.
facts.quote: La presencia de la fenestra mandibular externa en forma de óvalo es una particularidad de este género entre los atoposáuridos.

facts.statement: Both species of Knoetschkesuchus possess two types of teeth, a trait unique among atoposaurids.
facts.quote: Ambas especies de Knoetschkesuchus tienen dos tipos de dientes, algo único entre los atoposáuridos.

facts.statement: The first type of teeth found near the front of the jaw consists of conical pieces that are slightly constricted at the base and gently curved inward.
facts.quote: El primer tipo de dientes, hallado cerca del frente de la mandíbula, corresponde a piezas cónicas, apenas constreñidas en la base, y levemente curvadas hacia adentro.

facts.statement: The pseudocanine teeth, which are the fourth and fifth maxillary teeth, are elongated (nearly double the size of other maxillary teeth), sharper, and more compressed at the base.
facts.quote: Los dientes pseudocaniniformes, los cuales son el cuarto y quinto dientes maxilares, están alargados (con cerca del doble del tamaño de los otros dientes maxilares), más aguzados, y más comprimidos en la base.

facts.statement: In K. guimarotae all tooth tips are sharp, whereas in K. langenbergensis they gradually become blunter.
facts.quote: En K. guimarotae todas las puntas son afiladas, pero en K. langenbergensis estas se vuelven gradualmente más romas.

facts.statement: In total, K. guimarotae had at least 15 maxillary teeth, while K. langenbergensis had 17 or 18.
facts.quote: En total, K. guimarotae tenía al menos 15 dientes maxilares, y K. langenbergensis 17 o 18.

facts.statement: Being relatively small, Knoetschkesuchus likely fed primarily on invertebrates and possibly small vertebrates, including amphibians and mammals.
facts.quote: Al ser relativamente pequeño, Knoetschkesuchus se debió de haber alimentado principalmente de invertebrados y posiblemente pequeños vertebrados (incluyendo anfibios y mamíferos).

facts.statement: The parent group of Knoetschkesuchus is the family Atoposauridae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Atoposauridae

facts.statement: Knoetschkesuchus is classified within the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: Knoetschkesuchus lived during the Kimmeridgian to Tithonian stages, between 154.8 and 145.06 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Kimmeridgian to Tithonian (154.8 to 145.06 million years ago)
